title: Systems at Scale
subtitle: How the big ones were built
summary: In 2003 LiveJournal's database could not keep up, so Brad Fitzpatrick wrote a cache that lived in the spare memory of its web servers. Most large systems grew like that, one bottleneck at a time. The course follows them from Google's file system, built on disks expected to fail daily, through Amazon's shopping cart that had to accept items during an outage, to Spanner, which put GPS receivers and atomic clocks in its datacentres. The numbers come first: how long a disk seek takes, how many machines one search touches, what retries do to a struggling service. Branches serve a map of the world and find the nearest car, and a design studio works through chat, a ticket sale and a fleet update.
